newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bondi Beach murder suspect wins bail.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bondi Beach murder suspect wins bail.

text.p: The man accused of beating to death a British tourist near Sydney's Bondi Beach last month was granted bail on Friday but ordered to observe a night curfew and not drink alcohol.

The New South Wales Supreme Court ruled that Aaron Martin, charged with the murder of London postman Brian Hagland, would have to be accompanied by a relative if he went out and should attend Alcoholics Anonymous meetings at least weekly.
Hagland's fiancee said he was the victim of an unprovoked and brutal attack by two men near Sydney's most famous beach on September 7.

Another man has been charged as an accessory to the murder. Martin's lawyer, Leigh Johnson, said he would be pleading not guilty to the charge and contesting that account. Martin, 22, followed the hearing via a video link from Long Bay Jail.
Prosecutor Chris Maxwell opposed Martin's bail application, describing him on Thursday as "a young man who seems to have an attraction for beating people up in public places".
Johnson admitted that he had been involved in a scuffle with Hagland, but argued that he should not be kept in prison pending his trial.
